name: Push-up - Full form
tip: Keep a straight line from head to heels; lower the chest between the hands without letting the shoulders shrug.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands just outside shoulder width and fingers spread.
Brace glutes and abdomen, bend the elbows about 30–45 degrees from the body, and lower under control.
Press the floor away until the elbows are straight while keeping chest and hips moving together.

name: Push-up - Incline
tip: Use a stable surface and keep the same rigid body line as a floor push-up.
instructions: Place hands on a secure bench or bar and walk the feet back into a straight plank.
Lower the chest to the support without dropping the hips or reaching the chin.
Press to straight arms; lower the support height only when every rep stays controlled.

name: Push-up - Knee
tip: Keep shoulders, hips and knees in one line; do not fold at the hips.
instructions: Kneel on a padded surface and place hands just outside shoulder width.
Brace the trunk and lower the chest between the hands with controlled elbows.
Press up as one unit without rocking back toward the heels.

name: Push-up - Decline
tip: Elevate the feet only as high as you can maintain stacked ribs and a neutral neck.
instructions: Place toes on a secure support and hands in normal push-up position.
Brace hard and lower the upper chest toward the floor.
Press evenly through both palms without sagging through the lower back.

name: Push-up - Wide
tip: Use only a moderately wider hand position and stop if the front of the shoulder feels pinched.
instructions: Set the hands wider than shoulder width with fingers forward or slightly out.
Lower under control while keeping shoulders away from the ears.
Press back to a rigid plank without bouncing at the bottom.

name: Push-up - Diamond
tip: Keep elbows tracking back and use a hand spacing that does not strain the wrists.
instructions: Place hands close beneath the sternum, forming a comfortable triangle with thumbs and fingers.
Lower the torso with elbows close to the ribs.
Press to full elbow extension while keeping the shoulders depressed.

name: Push-up - Archer
tip: Shift the chest toward the working hand while the other arm lengthens; keep both shoulders controlled.
instructions: Take a wide hand position and begin in a rigid plank.
Bend one elbow and move the chest toward that hand while the opposite arm straightens.
Press back to centre and alternate sides without rotating the hips.

name: Push-up - Typewriter
tip: Stay low while moving side to side; reduce range before the shoulders roll forward.
instructions: Lower into the bottom of a wide push-up toward one hand.
Keeping the chest low, shift across to the other hand as the first arm straightens.
Return to centre and press up, or continue smoothly if strength allows.

name: Push-up - Pike
tip: Drive the head forward and down between the hands so the shoulders, not the chest, take the load.
instructions: Start in an inverted V with hips high, hands shoulder width and heels lifted as needed.
Bend the elbows back and lower the crown of the head toward a point just ahead of the hands.
Press the floor away and return the shoulders over the hands without losing the high-hip position.

name: Push-up - Pike, feet elevated
tip: Stack the hips above the shoulders as much as mobility permits and keep the head path forward of the hands.
instructions: Place feet on a stable box and hands shoulder width on the floor.
Lift the hips, brace the ribs down, and lower the head slowly between the hands.
Press back to straight arms; reduce box height if the back arches or elbows flare.

name: Push-up - Pseudo planche
tip: Turn the hands slightly out if needed and lean only as far as the wrists and elbows remain comfortable.
instructions: Set hands near the hips with fingers forward or slightly outward and protract the shoulder blades.
Lean the shoulders ahead of the wrists, then lower while keeping elbows close.
Press back without losing the forward lean or hollow-body position.

name: Push-up - Hindu
tip: Move smoothly through the shoulders and spine; never force the low-back extension.
instructions: Begin in a high-hip downward-dog position.
Bend the elbows and sweep the chest low and forward between the hands.
Finish with the chest lifted, then reverse the path or push back to the start.

name: Push-up - Explosive
tip: End the set as soon as hand clearance or a rigid landing deteriorates.
instructions: Start in a braced push-up position and descend under control.
Drive forcefully through the palms so the hands leave the floor.
Land softly with elbows unlocked, absorb the force, and reset before the next rep.

name: Push-up - One-arm assisted
tip: Use the support hand only as much as needed and keep the hips square.
instructions: Place the working hand under the shoulder and the assistance hand on a raised block or wide to the side.
Widen the feet, brace, and lower toward the working hand without twisting.
Press through the working arm; progressively reduce assistance over time.

name: Push-up - One-arm
tip: Use a wide foot stance, resist torso rotation and stop before the shoulder rolls inward.
instructions: Place one hand beneath the shoulder, spread the feet wide and keep the free hand behind the back or at the hip.
Brace the entire body and lower toward the planted hand with the elbow tracking back.
Press to full extension while keeping hips and shoulders as square as possible.

name: Pull-up - Full form
tip: Start from an active hang, drive elbows toward the ribs and avoid kicking or craning the neck.
instructions: Grip the bar just outside shoulder width and begin from a dead hang.
Depress the shoulder blades, brace the hollow body, and pull until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to straight elbows before the next rep.

name: Chin-up - Full form
tip: Keep the ribs down and let the elbows travel toward the hips rather than curling only with the arms.
instructions: Take a shoulder-width underhand grip and hang with straight elbows.
Set the shoulder blades and pull the chest toward the bar without swinging.
Pause briefly above the bar, then lower to a full controlled hang.

name: Pull-up - Neutral grip
tip: Keep forearms parallel and shoulders depressed; use the full pain-free range.
instructions: Hang from parallel handles with palms facing each other.
Brace and pull by driving the elbows down beside the torso.
Lower slowly until the elbows are straight and shoulders remain controlled.

name: Pull-up - Wide grip
tip: Use a modestly wide grip; excessive width shortens range and can irritate shoulders.
instructions: Grip outside shoulder width and establish an active hang.
Pull the upper chest toward the bar while keeping the ribs controlled.
Lower without dropping suddenly into the shoulders.

name: Pull-up - Scapular
tip: Keep elbows straight and move only through controlled shoulder-blade elevation and depression.
instructions: Hang with straight arms and a braced trunk.
Pull the shoulder blades down so the body rises a few centimetres.
Pause, then return slowly to a relaxed but controlled hang.

name: Pull-up - Band assisted
tip: Use the lightest assistance that allows a smooth full range without bouncing from the band.
instructions: Secure the band safely and place a foot or knee into it.
Begin from a full hang, brace, and pull with the same path as an unassisted rep.
Lower slowly and keep tension controlled when entering or leaving the band.

name: Pull-up - Negative
tip: Own the entire descent for 3–8 seconds; step back to the top instead of jumping repeatedly.
instructions: Use a box to begin with chin above the bar and shoulders set.
Remove the feet and lower evenly through the full range for the planned time.
Place the feet back on the box before resetting for the next rep.

name: Pull-up - Chest to bar
tip: Pull the elbows behind the torso and meet the bar with the chest without throwing the head forward.
instructions: Start from an active hollow-body hang.
Pull strongly and continue past chin height until the lower chest approaches the bar.
Control the descent and reset the shoulder blades between reps.

name: Pull-up - Sternum
tip: Lean back only enough to bring the sternum toward the bar while keeping the movement controlled.
instructions: Begin from an active hang with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Pull high while opening the chest and driving elbows down and slightly behind.
Touch or approach the lower sternum, then descend smoothly without swinging.

name: Pull-up - False grip
tip: Keep the wrist over the bar or ring and build tolerance gradually; stop for wrist pinching.
instructions: Place the heel of each palm over the bar or ring with wrists flexed.
Maintain the false grip as you pull through a full controlled range.
Lower without letting the hand roll back to a normal grip.

name: Pull-up - Archer
tip: Pull toward one hand while the opposite arm lengthens; avoid rotating the pelvis.
instructions: Take a wide overhand grip and begin from an active hang.
Pull the chest toward one hand while extending the other arm along the bar.
Lower to centre under control and alternate sides.

name: Pull-up - L-sit
tip: Keep legs lifted with the pelvis tucked; reduce to a tuck rather than swinging.
instructions: Hang actively and raise straight legs to hip height, or use a tucked knee position.
Maintain compression while pulling until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control without letting the legs drop between reps.

name: Pull-up - Weighted
tip: Secure the load, eliminate momentum and keep every rep at the same full range.
instructions: Attach a belt or hold a light load securely before taking the bar.
Start from an active hang and pull until the chin clearly passes the bar.
Lower under control; stop the set when range or body position changes.

name: Hang - Dead
tip: Let the arms lengthen while keeping enough shoulder control to avoid painful traction.
instructions: Grip the bar securely and lift the feet clear.
Breathe normally with straight elbows and a long spine.
Step down before grip failure or shoulder discomfort changes the position.

name: Hang - Active
tip: Depress the shoulder blades without bending the elbows or flaring the ribs.
instructions: Begin in a dead hang with straight arms.
Pull the shoulders away from the ears and lightly lift the chest.
Hold the active position while breathing, then lower with control.

name: Hang - False grip
tip: Build time slowly and keep the wrist position deliberate rather than letting it slip under fatigue.
instructions: Set the heel of the palm over the bar or rings with the wrist flexed.
Hang with shoulders controlled and the grip maintained on both sides.
Step down before the wrist rolls out of position or feels pinched.

name: Row - Inverted
tip: Keep the body rigid and pull the lower chest to the bar without shrugging.
instructions: Set a secure waist-height bar and hang beneath it with straight arms.
Brace glutes and abdomen, then pull shoulder blades back and elbows toward the ribs.
Touch the chest to the bar if possible and lower to straight arms under control.

name: Row - Inverted, feet elevated
tip: Keep heels, hips and shoulders in one line; lower the feet if the hips sag.
instructions: Place heels on a stable support and grip the row bar with straight arms.
Brace the entire body and pull the chest toward the bar.
Pause at the top, then lower without losing the straight body line.

name: Row - Rings
tip: Keep rings close to the ribs and finish with shoulders down, not rolled forward.
instructions: Hold the rings and walk the feet forward to the required body angle.
Brace, retract the shoulder blades and pull the rings toward the lower ribs.
Rotate naturally if comfortable and lower to full arm extension.

name: Row - Rings archer
tip: Pull one ring to the ribs while the other arm opens; keep both rings under tension.
instructions: Set a moderately inclined ring-row position.
Pull toward one ring while extending the opposite arm out to the side.
Return slowly and alternate without twisting the hips.

name: Dip - Full form
tip: Keep shoulders depressed and use only the depth that stays smooth and pain-free.
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight elbows and shoulders down.
Lean slightly forward, bend the elbows back, and lower until the upper arm is about parallel or your safe depth.
Press to full support without bouncing or shrugging at the top.

name: Dip - Band assisted
tip: Use the band for consistent assistance and do not rebound from its stretch.
instructions: Secure a band across the bars and place knees or feet on it safely.
Lower with shoulders depressed and elbows tracking back.
Press smoothly to support and control the band when entering or leaving.

name: Dip - Negative
tip: Use a 3–6 second descent and step back to the top before form breaks.
instructions: Start in a stable straight-arm support using a box if needed.
Lower slowly with elbows tracking back and shoulders controlled.
Place feet on the box at your safe bottom depth and reset.

name: Dip - Straight bar
tip: Keep the bar close to the body and finish with the torso balanced over it.
instructions: Begin supported above a straight bar with hands just outside the hips.
Lean over the bar and lower the chest while elbows bend behind you.
Press down until the elbows are straight without letting the bar drift away.

name: Dip - Rings
tip: Keep rings close and externally rotated at support; master a steady hold before deep reps.
instructions: Begin in ring support with elbows straight, rings beside the hips and shoulders down.
Lower slowly while keeping forearms controlled and rings close.
Press to support and turn the ring faces slightly forward only if stable.

name: Dip - Weighted
tip: Secure the load and keep the same pain-free depth on every rep.
instructions: Attach the load securely and establish a stable parallel-bar support.
Lower with shoulders depressed and a controlled slight forward lean.
Press to straight arms without swinging the weight or bouncing.

name: Dip - Russian
tip: Learn on low bars with assistance; the forearm transition should be smooth and never forced through wrist or elbow pain.
instructions: Lower from support until the forearms contact the bars under control.
Shift the shoulders forward and roll from forearms back onto the hands.
Press to support, using a band or feet as needed until the transition is quiet and repeatable.

name: Dip - Isometric bottom hold
tip: Hold only at a shoulder depth that feels stable; breathe and stop for pinching.
instructions: Lower into the chosen dip depth with shoulders away from the ears.
Hold the joint angle without sinking or bouncing.
Press or step safely out before alignment changes.

name: Muscle-up - Jumping transition
tip: Use a low bar and legs only enough to practise a close, smooth turnover.
instructions: Set a bar around chest height and grip it with feet on the floor.
Jump lightly as you pull the chest over the bar and roll the wrists into support.
Lower through the same close transition under control.

name: Muscle-up - Band assisted
tip: Keep the bar close and reduce band assistance only when the transition remains controlled.
instructions: Secure the band and enter it carefully with an overhand or appropriate false grip.
Pull high, bring the chest over the bar and press through the straight-bar dip.
Reverse the transition slowly and avoid a large uncontrolled kip.

name: Muscle-up - Negative
tip: Move slowly through the transition; stop if the wrist, elbow or front of shoulder pinches.
instructions: Use a box to begin in stable straight-bar support.
Lower through the dip and rotate the chest behind the bar over 3–5 seconds.
Continue into a controlled pull-up descent and step back to the top.

name: Muscle-up - Strict bar
tip: Pull high with minimal swing and keep the bar close through the turnover.
instructions: Start from an active hang with a firm overhand grip and braced hollow body.
Pull explosively toward the lower chest, then lean over the bar as the wrists turn.
Finish the straight-bar dip to full support and descend under control.

name: Muscle-up - Strict rings
tip: Maintain the false grip and keep rings tight to the torso throughout the transition.
instructions: Begin in a false-grip hang with rings close and shoulders active.
Pull rings to the chest, lean forward and trace them beneath the armpits into the dip bottom.
Press to ring support, then reverse every phase under control.

name: Support hold - False-grip transition
tip: Use a low bar, rings or band so the exact transition angle can be held without joint pinching.
instructions: Set the false grip and support enough bodyweight to place hands near the transition point.
Keep wrists fixed, elbows close and shoulders depressed while breathing.
Step out before grip or wrist position changes.

name: Handstand - Chest to wall
tip: Push tall through the shoulders, tuck the ribs and keep only the toes lightly touching the wall.
instructions: Walk the feet up the wall and hands inward until the body is nearly vertical.
Spread the fingers, push the floor away and squeeze glutes with ribs tucked.
Hold while breathing, then walk down before the shoulders or wrists lose position.

name: Handstand - Back to wall
tip: Use the wall as a light balance check, not a surface to arch against.
instructions: Kick up gently with hands shoulder width and heels near the wall.
Stack wrists, elbows, shoulders, hips and ankles while pushing tall.
Peel one heel away at a time to practise balance, then exit with control.

name: Handstand - Freestanding practice
tip: Use the fingertips as brakes, keep the gaze between the hands and practise safe exits before long attempts.
instructions: Place hands shoulder width, kick one leg up softly and bring the legs together over the hips.
Push tall, squeeze glutes and use fingertip pressure to correct overbalance.
Pirouette or cartwheel out rather than fighting a failed position.

name: Handstand - Wall walk
tip: Move in short controlled steps and keep the trunk braced so the lower back does not collapse.
instructions: Start in a plank with feet against the wall.
Walk feet upward and hands toward the wall while continually pushing the floor away.
Pause in a controlled chest-to-wall position, then reverse every step to the floor.

name: Handstand - Wall shoulder tap
tip: Shift weight through the supporting palm before lifting the other hand; keep hips quiet.
instructions: Set a stable wall handstand with feet lightly supported.
Shift the shoulders over one hand and briefly touch the opposite shoulder.
Replace the hand softly and alternate without twisting or collapsing.

name: Handstand push-up - Wall partial range
tip: Use a pad or target to standardise depth and keep elbows angled back rather than flared wide.
instructions: Kick or walk into a stable wall handstand with hands shoulder width.
Lower slowly until the head touches the raised target while maintaining shoulder control.
Press to straight arms and push tall before the next rep.

name: Handstand push-up - Wall full range
tip: Create a tripod head position slightly ahead of the hands and never bounce from the floor.
instructions: Set a stable wall handstand with hands shoulder width and ribs controlled.
Lower the crown of the head to a point just ahead of the hands over 2–4 seconds.
Press through the palms to full elbow extension and finish tall through the shoulders.

name: Handstand push-up - Wall negative
tip: Use a 3–5 second descent and come down after each rep instead of pressing from a failed depth.
instructions: Begin in a stable wall handstand with elbows straight.
Lower the head forward between the hands at a constant slow speed.
Place the head softly on a pad, exit safely and reset for the next rep.

name: Handstand push-up - Deficit wall
tip: Increase depth in small increments only after full-range wall reps are strong and pain-free.
instructions: Place secure parallettes or blocks evenly and enter a stable wall handstand.
Lower the shoulders below hand level through a controlled pain-free range.
Press to full support without losing the stacked trunk position.

name: Handstand push-up - Freestanding
tip: Balance first, then bend; abandon the rep early enough to use a practised safe exit.
instructions: Establish a quiet freestanding handstand and shift slightly forward into the fingertip balance zone.
Lower into a tripod shape with the head ahead of the hands and elbows controlled.
Press vertically while correcting balance through palms and fingertips.

name: Planche - Lean
tip: Protract strongly, lock the elbows and lean only as far as wrists and elbows stay completely comfortable.
instructions: Start in a high plank with fingers spread and elbows turned forward.
Round the upper back, depress the shoulders and shift them gradually ahead of the wrists.
Hold a hollow body without bending the arms, then rock back before alignment changes.

name: Planche - Frog stand
tip: Use the knees on the arms for assistance and look slightly forward rather than dropping the head.
instructions: Squat, place hands shoulder width and rest knees high on the upper arms.
Lean forward until the feet float while gripping the floor with the fingers.
Hold with controlled shoulders, then place one foot down at a time.

name: Planche - Tuck
tip: Keep the upper back rounded, elbows locked and knees pulled tightly toward the chest.
instructions: Place hands or parallettes beside the hips and protract the shoulder blades.
Lean forward, press down and lift both feet with knees tucked tightly.
Maintain straight arms and hips clear of the support, then lower under control.

name: Planche - Advanced tuck
tip: Open the hip angle gradually while keeping the back rounded and shoulders ahead of the hands.
instructions: Establish a stable tuck planche with locked elbows and strong protraction.
Move the knees away from the chest and flatten the back slightly without dropping the hips.
Hold the longest lever that remains motionless, then return to tuck before lowering.

name: Planche - Single leg
tip: Keep the pelvis level and switch sides; do not twist toward the extended leg.
instructions: Begin from an advanced tuck planche.
Extend one leg behind while maintaining locked elbows and protraction.
Hold both sides for equal clean time, then tuck before returning the feet.

name: Planche - Straddle
tip: Widening the legs shortens the lever, but the hips must remain level with the shoulders.
instructions: From advanced tuck, open both legs wide while leaning shoulders forward.
Lock knees, point toes and maintain strong scapular protraction.
Hold without sinking at the hips, then tuck before lowering.

name: Planche - Full
tip: Attempt only after the prior lever is repeatable on low-readiness days with no joint symptoms.
instructions: Establish a strong planche lean with elbows locked and shoulders protracted.
Extend both legs together until the body is horizontal from shoulders to toes.
Maintain a hollow line and leave the hold before any elbow bend or hip drop.

name: Support hold - Parallettes
tip: Push tall with elbows locked and shoulders depressed; do not hang passively between the arms.
instructions: Grip stable parallettes beside the hips and press to straight-arm support.
Lift or lightly assist the feet while keeping ribs stacked and shoulder blades controlled.
Hold with steady breathing and step down before the elbows soften.

name: Support hold - Rings
tip: Keep rings close to the hips and turn them only as far outward as stability allows.
instructions: Press into straight-arm support with rings beside the body.
Depress the shoulders, lock elbows and minimise ring movement.
Hold with a braced trunk, then lower safely before shaking becomes uncontrolled.

name: Front lever - Tuck
tip: Pull the bar toward the hips with straight arms and keep the lower back rounded.
instructions: Hang from the bar and depress the shoulder blades.
Tuck knees to the chest and rotate the body until the back is near horizontal.
Hold with straight elbows and hips lifted, then lower without swinging.

name: Front lever - Advanced tuck
tip: Open the hips while keeping the torso horizontal and shoulder blades depressed.
instructions: Begin in a solid tuck front lever.
Move knees away from the chest and flatten the back while pulling straight arms toward the hips.
Hold the longest clean shape and tuck again before lowering.

name: Front lever - Single leg
tip: Keep hips square and alternate legs for equal time.
instructions: Establish an advanced tuck front lever.
Extend one leg while the other knee remains tucked.
Maintain a horizontal torso and straight elbows, then switch sides.

name: Front lever - Straddle
tip: Open the legs without letting the hips fold or the shoulders rise toward the ears.
instructions: Pull into an advanced tuck with shoulders depressed.
Extend both knees and open the legs wide while keeping the hips level.
Hold with straight arms, then tuck before lowering.

name: Front lever - Full
tip: Keep a posterior pelvic tilt and pull the bar toward the hips through straight arms.
instructions: Begin from a controlled inverted or tucked position.
Extend both legs until the body forms one horizontal line.
Hold without hip sag or elbow bend, then return to tuck before lowering.

name: Back lever - Skin the cat
tip: Move slowly through a pain-free shoulder range and keep a way to place the feet down.
instructions: Hang from rings or a bar and lift the knees through the arms into an inverted tuck.
Lower the feet behind you while keeping elbows straight and shoulders controlled.
Reverse the path before the shoulders reach an uncomfortable range.

name: Back lever - Tuck
tip: Turn the elbows straight, keep the chest facing the floor and start with a tight tuck.
instructions: Move through skin-the-cat into an inverted tuck.
Lower the tucked body behind the arms until the back is horizontal.
Hold with locked elbows, then pull back to inverted before exiting.

name: Back lever - Advanced tuck
tip: Open the hips a little at a time without losing straight elbows or shoulder comfort.
instructions: Establish a stable tuck back lever.
Move knees away from the chest and extend the hips until the torso is horizontal.
Hold the clean lever, then tuck before returning to inverted.

name: Back lever - Straddle
tip: Keep the pelvis neutral and both elbows locked; stop immediately for front-shoulder strain.
instructions: From advanced tuck, extend and spread both legs.
Lower into a horizontal line while maintaining controlled shoulder extension.
Hold briefly, then tuck and return to inverted under control.

name: Back lever - Full
tip: Use rings if they allow a more comfortable shoulder rotation and never force the final range.
instructions: Start inverted with straight arms and a braced body.
Lower the fully extended body behind the arms until horizontal.
Hold with elbows locked and exit by returning to inverted or placing feet safely.

name: Hollow body - Hold
tip: Press the lower back into the floor; bend knees or raise arms if the back starts to arch.
instructions: Lie on the back, flatten the lower spine and tuck the pelvis.
Lift shoulders and legs while reaching arms overhead or forward.
Hold the lowest limb position that keeps the lower back fully connected to the floor.

name: Arch body - Hold
tip: Lengthen rather than lifting as high as possible; keep glutes active and neck neutral.
instructions: Lie face down with arms overhead and legs straight.
Brace glutes and lift hands, chest and thighs slightly from the floor.
Reach long through fingers and toes while breathing steadily.

name: Plank - Forearm
tip: Squeeze glutes and pull elbows toward the feet without moving them.
instructions: Place elbows under shoulders and extend the legs.
Tuck the pelvis slightly so head, hips and heels form one line.
Maintain steady breathing and stop before the lower back sags.

name: Plank - Side
tip: Keep shoulder away from the ear and hips stacked rather than rolling forward.
instructions: Support on one forearm beneath the shoulder with feet stacked or staggered.
Lift hips until the body forms a straight side line.
Hold while breathing, then lower with control and repeat the other side.

name: Raise - Hanging knee
tip: Curl the pelvis upward instead of only lifting the thighs; eliminate swinging.
instructions: Begin in an active hang with legs still.
Draw knees toward the chest and finish by tucking the pelvis.
Lower slowly to a motionless hang before the next rep.

name: Raise - Hanging straight leg
tip: Keep knees locked and use abdominal compression rather than momentum.
instructions: Hang actively with legs straight and slightly in front.
Raise the feet toward hip or bar height while curling the pelvis.
Lower for 2–3 seconds without swinging through the bottom.

name: Raise - Toes to bar
tip: Stay active through the shoulders and control the descent; do not chase contact with a large uncontrolled swing.
instructions: Hang with shoulders engaged and initiate a small hollow-body compression.
Lift straight legs and roll the pelvis until toes reach or approach the bar.
Lower under control and return to a stable hang.

name: L-sit - Tuck
tip: Push tall through straight arms and lift the knees using compression rather than leaning far back.
instructions: Support on parallettes or bars with elbows locked.
Depress the shoulders, tuck knees toward the chest and lift the feet.
Hold with hips between the hands, then lower softly.

name: L-sit - Full
tip: Lock the knees, point the toes and keep shoulders pushed down away from the ears.
instructions: Begin in straight-arm support and establish a strong tucked L-sit.
Extend both knees until the legs are horizontal.
Maintain a tall torso and controlled breathing before returning to tuck.

name: Compression - Seated leg lift
tip: Sit tall and lift from the hip flexors without rocking the trunk backward.
instructions: Sit with legs straight and hands beside the thighs or farther forward.
Press hands down, brace and lift one or both heels from the floor.
Pause at the top and lower quietly while keeping knees straight.

name: Squat - Air
tip: Keep the whole foot planted and let knees track in the same direction as the toes.
instructions: Stand around shoulder width with toes turned out as needed.
Sit hips down between the feet while keeping chest and arches controlled.
Drive through the whole foot to stand tall without the knees collapsing inward.

name: Squat - Jump
tip: Land quietly and finish the set when jump height or knee alignment drops.
instructions: Descend into a controlled quarter or half squat.
Drive through the floor and extend hips, knees and ankles to jump.
Land softly over the mid-foot, absorb into a squat and reset.

name: Split squat - Bodyweight
tip: Keep the front foot planted and lower the rear knee vertically rather than pitching forward.
instructions: Take a comfortable staggered stance with hips facing forward.
Bend both knees and lower until the rear knee approaches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to rise while keeping the pelvis level.

name: Split squat - Bulgarian
tip: Use a low rear-foot support and keep most of the load on the front leg.
instructions: Place the rear foot on a stable bench and set the front foot far enough forward for balance.
Lower the rear knee while the front knee tracks over the toes.
Press through the front foot to stand without pushing from the rear leg.

name: Pistol squat - Assisted
tip: Use the support for balance, keep the heel down and control the knee over the toes.
instructions: Hold a post, strap or rings lightly and lift one foot forward.
Sit down over the working heel through the deepest controlled range.
Use the leg to stand while reducing hand assistance over time.

name: Pistol squat - Full
tip: Maintain heel contact and knee alignment; use a counterweight if ankle mobility is the limiter.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other extended forward.
Sit the hips down while the working knee tracks over the toes and the heel stays planted.
Drive through the whole foot to return to standing without bouncing.

name: Nordic curl - Eccentric
tip: Keep hips extended and use the hands to catch before hamstring control is lost.
instructions: Kneel on padding with ankles secured by a reliable partner or anchor.
Squeeze glutes and lower the straight body forward as slowly as possible.
Catch with the hands, push lightly back and reset without wrenching the knees.

name: Glute bridge - Two leg
tip: Finish by squeezing glutes, not by arching the lower back.
instructions: Lie with knees bent and feet flat near the hips.
Tuck the pelvis slightly and drive through the heels to lift the hips.
Pause with ribs down, then lower the spine and hips under control.

name: Calf raise - Standing
tip: Use a full controlled stretch and pause at the top instead of bouncing.
instructions: Stand tall with the balls of the feet secure and a light balance support.
Lower heels through a comfortable stretch.
Rise as high as possible, pause, and lower slowly.

name: Bound - Lateral
tip: Stick each landing with the knee tracking over the foot before the next jump.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a small athletic bend.
Push sideways and land softly on the opposite leg.
Stabilise hip, knee and ankle for a clear pause, then bound back.

name: Wrist - Circles
tip: Move slowly through a comfortable range; circles are preparation, not a forced stretch.
instructions: Interlace fingers or hold hands loosely in front of the body.
Circle wrists smoothly in both directions for equal time.
Keep the movement pain-free and gradually increase range as tissues warm.

name: Wrist - Quadruped walks
tip: Keep some bodyweight in the knees and use small hand-angle changes without forcing end range.
instructions: Kneel on all fours with fingers forward and elbows straight but not jammed.
Shift weight gently forward, back and side to side, then turn hands incrementally outward.
Keep palms controlled and stop before pinching or sharp discomfort.

name: Wrist - Extension isometric
tip: Use moderate effort and a neutral forearm; tendon work should feel loaded, not sharp.
instructions: Rest the forearm on a bench with the hand just beyond the edge and palm down.
Hold a light weight with the wrist slightly extended.
Maintain the angle without movement, then lower the weight with the other hand if needed.

name: Wrist - Flexion isometric
tip: Keep the forearm still and choose a load that allows a steady, symptom-free hold.
instructions: Support the forearm with palm up and hand beyond the bench edge.
Hold a light weight with the wrist slightly flexed.
Maintain the position and relaxed grip, then lower under control.

name: Finger extension - Resistance band
tip: Open all fingers evenly and use high-quality easy repetitions rather than maximal resistance.
instructions: Loop a light band around the fingertips and bring them together.
Spread fingers and thumb apart against resistance.
Pause briefly, then return slowly without letting the band snap closed.

name: Scapular push-up - Straight arm
tip: Keep elbows locked and move the chest only by gliding the shoulder blades.
instructions: Take a high-plank or knee-plank position with straight arms.
Let shoulder blades move gently together without sagging the hips.
Push the floor away until the upper back rounds, then repeat slowly.

name: Scapular protraction - Hold
tip: Push the floor away and spread the shoulder blades without shrugging toward the ears.
instructions: Set a high plank, planche lean or straight-arm support.
Round the upper back by pressing strongly through the hands.
Maintain locked elbows and steady breathing for the planned hold.

name: Arm circle - Mobility
tip: Start small and increase the circle only while the ribs and neck stay relaxed.
instructions: Stand tall with arms extended comfortably to the sides.
Circle forward through a controlled range, then reverse.
Keep shoulders down and avoid arching the lower back.

name: Shoulder pass-through - Band
tip: Use a very wide grip and a light band; never force a painful point behind the body.
instructions: Hold a band wide in front with elbows straight.
Lift it overhead and continue behind only through a smooth shoulder range.
Return along the same path while keeping ribs controlled.

name: Stretch - Wrist extension
tip: Use gentle pressure through the palm and stop well before numbness, tingling or sharp pain.
instructions: Place palm on a bench or floor with fingers pointing forward or slightly back.
Keep the elbow straight and shift bodyweight gradually until a mild forearm stretch appears.
Hold without bouncing, then release and repeat the other side.

name: Stretch - Wrist flexion
tip: The pressure should be mild across the top of the forearm, never forced through the wrist joint.
instructions: Extend one arm with palm facing down and gently curl the fingers toward the forearm.
Use the other hand to add light pressure while keeping the elbow straight.
Hold, release slowly and repeat the other side.

name: Stretch - Lat on bench
tip: Keep ribs tucked and sink the chest rather than forcing the lower back into extension.
instructions: Kneel facing a bench and place elbows or hands on it.
Sit hips back and lower the chest between the arms.
Breathe into the sides of the ribs, then return slowly.

name: Stretch - Chest doorway
tip: Use a low-to-moderate arm angle and turn the body gently without pushing the shoulder forward.
instructions: Place the forearm on a door frame with elbow around shoulder height or lower.
Step through and rotate the torso away until a mild chest stretch appears.
Keep the shoulder blade controlled, hold, then change sides.

name: Stretch - Shoulder flexion at wall
tip: Keep ribs down and move from the shoulders; do not compensate with a large back arch.
instructions: Place hands or forearms on a wall slightly above shoulder height.
Step back and hinge, letting the chest move between the arms.
Maintain gentle pressure and steady breathing, then rise slowly.

name: Squat - Barbell back
tip: Brace before descending, keep pressure over the mid-foot and use a repeatable depth.
instructions: Set the bar securely across the upper back and take a stable stance.
Brace, sit between the hips and let knees track with the toes.
Drive through the whole foot to stand without losing trunk position.

name: Deadlift - Romanian
tip: Hinge at the hips with soft knees, keep the load close and stop before the back rounds.
instructions: Stand tall with the weight against the thighs and brace the trunk.
Push hips back while sliding the load down the legs.
When hamstrings limit the hinge, drive hips forward to stand.

name: Press - Barbell overhead
tip: Squeeze glutes, keep ribs down and move the head through after the bar clears.
instructions: Hold the bar at the upper chest with wrists stacked over elbows.
Brace and press vertically while moving the head slightly back.
Finish with the bar over the middle of the foot, then lower under control.

name: Row - Weighted
tip: Brace first, pull the elbow toward the hip and control the full return.
instructions: Set a stable hinged or supported torso position with arms extended.
Pull the weight toward the lower ribs without twisting or shrugging.
Pause briefly and lower until the shoulder blade can protract under control.

name: Curl - Biceps
tip: Keep upper arms still and avoid swinging the torso to finish the rep.
instructions: Stand or sit tall with elbows near the sides.
Curl through the full comfortable range without moving the shoulders forward.
Lower for 2–3 seconds to straight elbows.

name: Raise - Dumbbell lateral
tip: Lead with the elbows, use a light load and stop before the traps dominate.
instructions: Hold light weights by the sides with a soft elbow bend.
Raise arms in the scapular plane to around shoulder height.
Lower slowly without swinging through the bottom.

name: Pushdown - Triceps
tip: Keep elbows fixed by the sides and control the return.
instructions: Stand braced at the cable with elbows bent and tucked.
Extend the elbows until arms are straight without moving the shoulders.
Return slowly while keeping upper arms still.

name: Carry - Farmer's
tip: Stand tall with ribs stacked over pelvis and take deliberate even steps.
instructions: Pick up equal secure loads with a braced hinge.
Walk tall with shoulders controlled and minimal side-to-side sway.
Turn carefully and set the loads down with the same braced hinge.

name: Bike - Static HIIT
tip: Set resistance before the interval and keep knees tracking straight during hard efforts.
instructions: Warm up progressively and adjust the seat so the knee remains slightly bent at the bottom.
Alternate planned hard efforts with easy pedalling while maintaining smooth cadence.
Cool down until breathing and heart rate settle.

name: Skipping - Freestyle
tip: Mix only rope patterns you can perform with quiet, repeatable landings.
instructions: Begin with basic bounce until the rope rhythm is settled.
Rotate through comfortable patterns such as boxer step, side-to-side and high knees without chasing speed.
Return to basic bounce whenever timing or landing control starts to break down.

name: Skipping - Basic
tip: Jump only high enough to clear the rope and land quietly under the hips.
instructions: Stand tall with elbows near the sides and turn the rope from the wrists.
Use small two-foot jumps on the balls of the feet.
Keep shoulders relaxed and stop when landings become heavy.

name: Skipping - Boxer step
tip: Shift weight softly side to side while keeping the rope rhythm steady.
instructions: Begin with basic low jumps and relaxed wrist turns.
Alternate pressure between feet with a small side-to-side weight shift.
Keep the torso tall and land quietly throughout.

name: Skipping - High knees
tip: Maintain posture and rope rhythm; reduce knee height before landings become heavy.
instructions: Start with a basic skip and stable cadence.
Alternate lifting knees toward hip height while the opposite foot jumps.
Keep the contacts quick and finish before posture collapses.

name: Skipping - Forward and back
tip: Use very small travel and keep both feet beneath the centre of mass.
instructions: Establish basic two-foot skipping.
Hop a few centimetres forward on one turn and back on the next.
Maintain quiet landings and consistent wrist rhythm.

name: Push-up - Weighted
tip: Secure the load over the upper back, keep a rigid trunk and stop if it shifts during the set.
instructions: Set the load securely with help or use a fitted vest before taking a high plank.
Lower chest and hips together through the normal full-form push-up path.
Press to straight arms without sagging or letting the load move toward the neck.

name: Pull-up - Bodyweight back-off
tip: Use full controlled range and leave one or two repetitions in reserve when form slows.
instructions: After heavier pulling, take a normal full-form overhand hang.
Pull without momentum until the chin clears the bar.
Lower to straight elbows and end the set before range shortens.

name: Dip - Bodyweight back-off
tip: Use the same shoulder-controlled depth on every rep and stop before the support position deteriorates.
instructions: Establish a tall parallel-bar support after heavier dip work.
Lower smoothly to the usual pain-free depth with elbows tracking back.
Press to straight arms and leave one or two clean reps in reserve.

name: Isometric hold - Wall squat or dip bottom
tip: Choose one clearly recorded position, breathe steadily and stop for sharp or joint-localised pain.
instructions: Set either a stable wall-squat angle or a controlled pain-free dip depth.
Hold the selected joint angle without bouncing, sinking or breath-holding.
Exit deliberately before alignment changes and record which variation was used.

name: Pull-up - Isometric hold
tip: Record the hold position—top, mid-range or active hang—and keep shoulders controlled throughout.
instructions: Step or pull into the chosen repeatable pull-up angle.
Hold without kicking, shrugging or letting the elbows drift.
Lower under control before the position changes and use a box to reset.

name: Push-up - Isometric hold
tip: Choose a repeatable pain-free depth and keep chest and hips aligned while breathing.
instructions: Lower a rigid plank to the chosen push-up angle.
Hold with elbows tracking back and shoulder blades controlled.
Press up or place knees down before the trunk sags.

name: Dip - Isometric hold
tip: Hold only in a shoulder position that remains stable and free of pinching.
instructions: Lower from support to a clearly recorded dip angle.
Maintain depressed shoulders, controlled elbows and steady breathing.
Press or step out before the body sinks below the chosen position.

name: Pull-up - Rings
tip: Let the rings rotate naturally while keeping them close and the shoulders depressed.
instructions: Hang from rings with straight elbows and establish an active shoulder position.
Pull the rings toward the ribs, rotating toward a neutral or underhand finish as comfortable.
Lower slowly to full arm extension without swinging.

name: Push-up - Rings
tip: Keep rings close to the body and use a height that lets the shoulders remain stable.
instructions: Set rings evenly and take a rigid plank with straight arms.
Lower the chest between the rings while keeping elbows controlled.
Press the rings down and inward to return to support without letting them drift apart.
